units.en: Moreover, the writ contains the character 'ji,' the temple taboo of Emperor Xuanzong; although ordinary edicts do not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a descendant in succession and we do not wish to pronounce the taboos of successive sages—'ji' is now changed to 'zong.'"
units.literal: Moreover, within the writ text is the character 'ji,' which is the temple taboo of Emperor Xuanzong; although ordinary edicts do not avoid it, the Lesser Emperor is a descendant in succession and we do not wish to pronounce the taboos of successive sages—now 'ji' is changed to the character 'zong."

units.zh: 今昭宣上去玄宗十四世，奏改冊文，非典故也。）〉
units.en: From the August and Illustrious up to Emperor Xuanzong are fourteen generations; memorializing a change to the writ text is not according to precedent.)〉
units.literal: Now from the August and Illustrious up to Emperor Xuanzong are fourteen generations; to memorialize changing the writ text is not according to precedent.)〉

units.zh: 伏詳本朝列聖之舊典，明皇定禮之新規，開元十年，特立九廟，子孫遵守，歷代無虧。
units.en: We have examined the old statutes of our dynasty's successive emperors and the new ritual regulations established under Emperor Ming; in Kaiyuan 10 nine temples were specially established, and descendants have observed this through the generations without lapse.
units.literal: Your subjects have examined in detail the old statutes of the successive sage emperors of this dynasty and the new regulations for fixing ritual under Emperor Ming; in the tenth year of Kaiyuan nine temples were specially established, observed by descendants through the generations without impairment.

units.zh: 唐初悉用祝版，唯陵廟用玉冊，玄皇親祭郊廟，用玉為冊。
units.en: Early Tang used prayer boards exclusively; only imperial tombs and temples used jade tablets, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade tablets were employed.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tang all used prayer boards; only imperial tombs and temples used jade tablets, and when the August Sovereign personally sacrificed at suburban altars and temples, jade was used for tablets.

units.zh: 聖朝中興，重修宗廟，今太廟見饗高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗、獻祖、太祖、莊宗七廟，太祖景皇帝在祧廟之數，不列廟饗。
units.en: After the dynasty's revival the ancestral shrines were rebuilt; the Imperial Temple now served seven halls—the High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Yizong, Zhaozong, Xianzu, Taizu, and Zhuangzong—while Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing was relegated to the distant-lineage shrine and no longer received regular temple offerings.
units.literal: When the sacred court restored the dynasty and rebuilt the ancestral temples, the Imperial Ancestral Temple now offers sacrifices to seven temples: the High Ancestor, Great Ancestor, Yizong, Zhaozong, Xianzu, Taizu, and Zhuangzong. The Grand Ancestor Emperor Jing is counted among the distant ancestral temples and is not listed for temple sacrifice.

units.zh: 如或以玉難辦，寧小其制度，以取其真。」
units.en: If jade is hard to obtain, it is better to reduce the prescribed dimensions than sacrifice authenticity."
units.literal: If jade is difficult to obtain, it is better to reduce the scale of the regulations so as to preserve authenticity."

units.zh: 至如國朝，太祖曰景皇帝，以受命而有唐室，宣宗皇帝以隔代承運，皇綱復振故也。
units.en: In our dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuanzong because he received the fortune across generations and restored the imperial norm.
units.literal: As for our dynasty, the Grand Ancestor is called Emperor Jing because he received the Mandate and possessed the Tang house; Emperor Xuanzong because he received the fortune across generations and the imperial norm was restored.

units.zh: 元載以罪誅，除揆睦州刺史，入拜國子祭酒、禮部尚書，為盧杞所惡。
units.en: After Yuan Zai was executed for his crimes, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou. He later entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites, but Lu Qi bore him ill will.
units.literal: When Yuan Zai was executed for crime, Kui was appointed prefect of Muzhou; he entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education and Minister of Rites, but was hated by Lu Qi.

units.zh: 唐興，因隋樂不改，及黃巢之亂，樂縣散失，太常博士殷盈孫以周法鑄穀鐘、編鐘，處士蕭承訓等校石磐，合而奏之。
units.en: When the Tang rose, they retained Sui music unchanged. During Huang Chao's rebellion the court instruments were scattered and lost. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun recast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, while the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others retuned stone chimes, and the restored ensemble was played together once more.
units.literal: When the Tang rose, they took over Sui music without change; at the turmoil of Huang Chao the musical stands were scattered and lost; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician Yin Yingsun cast grain bells and chime-bells by Zhou methods, and the reclusive scholar Xiao Chengxun and others tuned stone chimes, and together they were played.

units.zh: 劉晏，字士安，曹州南華人。
units.en: Liu Yan, styled Shi'an, came from Nanhua in Caozhou.
units.literal: Liu Yan, courtesy name Shi'an, was a native of Nanhua in Caozhou.

units.zh: 時顏真卿以文學正直出為利州刺史，晏舉真卿自代為戶部，乃加國子祭酒。
units.en: When Yan Zhenqing, admired for scholarship and integrity, had been posted to Lizhou, Liu Yan proposed that Zhenqing succeed him at the Ministry of Revenue and was himself made chancellor of the national university in addition.
units.literal: At that time Yan Zhenqing, known for literary learning and uprightness, had been sent out as prefect of Lizhou; Yan recommended Zhenqing to succeed him in the Revenue Ministry, and Yan was additionally made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

units.zh: 年七歲，舉神童，授秘書省正字。
units.en: At seven he was nominated as a precocious youth and made Regular Scribe in the Secretariat.
units.literal: At age seven he was recommended as a child prodigy and appointed Regular Scribe of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 歷殿中侍御史，遷度支郎中、杭隴華三州刺史，尋遷河南尹。
units.en: He held the post of palace attendant censor, then rose to vice director of the revenue bureau and prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua, and shortly afterward became Intendant of the Henan circuit.
units.literal: He served as Attendant Censor in the Palace, was promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Revenue, and became prefect of Hang, Long, and Hua; soon after he was transferred to Intendant of Henan.

units.zh: 寶應二年，遷吏部尚書、平章事，領度支鹽鐵轉運租庸使。
units.en: In 763 he became minister of civil appointments and chief minister, continuing to head the combined revenue, salt, iron, transport, and corvée administration.
units.literal: In the second year of Baoying he was transferred to Minister of Personnel and made Grand Councilor, while retaining his posts as Commissioner for Revenue, Salt, Iron, Transport, and the Corvée Tax.

units.zh: 累授夏縣令，有能名。
units.en: Through successive appointments he became magistrate of Xia County and became known for administrative ability.
units.literal: He was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Xia County and gained a reputation for competence.

units.zh: 晏受命後，以轉運為己任，凡所經歷，必究利病之由。
units.en: Once charged with the task, Yan treated grain transport as his own mission and wherever he went traced every cause of waste or efficiency.
units.literal: After Yan received his mandate, he made transport his personal responsibility, and wherever he traveled he thoroughly investigated the causes of profit and harm.

units.zh: 時史朝義盜據東都，寄理長水。
units.en: With Shi Chaoyi holding the Eastern Capital, Yan governed from Changshui as his provisional seat.
units.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi was occupying the Eastern Capital by force, so he administered affairs from Changshui.

units.zh: 入為京兆尹，頃之，加戶部侍郎、兼御史中丞，判度支，委府事於司錄張群、杜亞，綜大體，議論號為稱職。
units.en: Recalled to serve as metropolitan governor of Chang'an, he soon added the titles of vice minister of revenue and concurrent vice censor-in-chief, with charge of the revenue bureau. He left routine office work to Zhang Qun and Du Ya as recorders while he kept the broad direction in hand, and contemporaries judged his policy judgments sound.
units.literal: He entered the capital as Metropolitan Governor; shortly thereafter he was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, with charge of revenue; he entrusted administrative affairs to Clerks Zhang Qun and Du Ya, while he handled overall policy, and his deliberations were said to be competent.

units.zh: 復入為京兆尹、戶部侍郎，判度支。
units.en: He returned to Chang'an as metropolitan governor and vice minister of revenue, again supervising the revenue bureau.
units.literal: He was recalled to serve again as Metropolitan Governor and Vice Minister of Revenue, with charge of revenue.

units.zh: 無何，為酷吏敬羽所構，貶通州刺史。
units.en: Not long after, the notorious official Jing Yu engineered charges against him, and he was demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.
units.literal: Before long he was framed by the harsh official Jing Yu and demoted to prefect of Tongzhou.

units.zh: 坐與中官程元振交通，元振得罪，晏罷相，為太子賓客。
units.en: Charged with ties to the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen, he lost the premiership when Yuanzhen was disgraced and was appointed mentor to the crown prince.
units.literal: He was punished for associating with the eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen; when Yuanzhen fell from power, Yan was removed from the chancellorship and made Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 尋授御史大夫，領東都、河南、江淮、山南等道轉運租庸鹽鐵使如故。
units.en: He was soon made Censor-in-Chief while retaining his former commissions for transport, zu-yong taxes, salt, and iron over the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jianghuai, Shannan, and related circuits.
units.literal: Soon after he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and continued to hold his former posts as Transport Commissioner for the Eastern Capital, Henan, Jianghuai, Shan'nan, and other circuits, as well as Commissioner for the Corvée Tax, Salt, and Iron.

units.zh: 至江淮，以書遺元載曰：
units.en: Reaching Jianghuai, he wrote Yuan Zai:
units.literal: When he reached the Jianghuai region, he sent a letter to Yuan Zai saying:

units.zh: 浮於淮、泗，達於汴，入於河，西循底柱、硤石、少華，楚帆越客，直抵建章、長樂，此安社稷之奇策也。
units.en: Grain could float up the Huai and Si, reach Bian, enter the Yellow River, and run west past Dizhu, Xiaoshi, and Shaohua so that Chu and Yue shipping would berth straight at the imperial palaces—this was the bold plan to stabilize the dynasty.
units.literal: Floating on the Huai and Si, reaching Bian, entering the Yellow River, and proceeding west along Dizhu, Xiaoshi, and Shaohua—Chu sails and Yue merchants arriving straight at Jianzhang and Changle: this is the extraordinary stratagem to secure the state.

units.zh: 晏賓於東朝，猶有官謗，相公終始故舊，不信流言，賈誼復召宣室，弘羊重興功利，敢不悉力以答所知。
units.en: Though as a guest at the Eastern Court I still face official slander, you have remained my old friend from first to last and will not heed idle talk. Just as Jia Yi was called back to the privy chamber and Sang Hongyang was trusted again to manage state revenue, I dare not spare myself in repaying your confidence.
units.literal: Yan, though favored at the Eastern Court, still bore official slander; the Chancellor had been my friend from first to last—do not believe wandering rumors; Jia Yi was summoned again to the Xuan Chamber, and Sang Hongyang revived profit and utility—how dare I not exert every effort to repay one who knows me?

units.zh: 驅馬陜郊，見三門渠津遺跡。
units.en: Traveling through the lands west of Shan, I found the remains of the Sanmen canal works.
units.literal: Riding through the Shaan suburbs, I saw the vestiges of the canals and crossings at Sanmen.

units.zh: 到河陰、鞏、洛，見宇文愷置梁公堰，分黃河水入通濟渠；
units.en: At Heyin, Gong, and Luoyang I inspected Yuwen Kai's weir diverting Yellow River water into the Tongji Canal;
units.literal: At Heyin, Gong, and Luo I saw how Yuwen Kai had built the Duke of Liang's weir to divide the Yellow River into the Tongji Canal;

units.zh: 大夫李傑新堤故事，飾像河廟，凜然如生。
units.en: and Li Jie's later embankment, with life-like images set up at the River God shrine.
units.literal: and the story of Censor-in-Chief Li Jie's new embankment, with statues adorned at the River Temple, stern as though living.

units.zh: 涉滎郊、浚澤，遙瞻淮甸，步步探討，知昔人用心，則潭、衡、桂陽必多積谷，關輔汲汲，只緣兵糧。
units.en: Passing through the Song riverland and dredging the marshes, scanning the Huai plain at every turn, I saw why the ancients labored as they did: the lake districts around Tan, Heng, and Guiyang must hold huge reserves, while Guanzhong starves chiefly for want of army rations.
units.literal: Crossing the Song suburbs and dredging marshes, gazing from afar at the Huai district, investigating step by step—I knew how our predecessors applied their minds: Tan, Heng, and Guiyang surely store abundant grain; the Guanzhong region strains only because of military grain.

units.zh: 漕引瀟、湘、洞庭，萬里幾日，淪波卦席，西指長安。
units.en: Once grain is floated down the Xiao, the Xiang, and Dongting Lake, ten thousand li can be covered in days, with sails quartering the waves all the way west to Chang'an.
units.literal: Transport by water from the Xiao and Xiang and Dongting—in a few days over ten thousand li—the waves rolling like mat patterns on deck, pointing west to Chang'an.

units.zh: 三秦之人，待此而飽；
units.en: The people of the Three Qin regions would at last eat their fill;
units.literal: The people of the Three Qins will rely on this to be fed;

units.zh: 六軍之眾，待此而強。
units.en: the imperial armies would grow strong on it.
units.literal: the masses of the Six Armies will rely on this to be strengthened.

units.zh: 天子無側席之憂，都人見泛舟之役；
units.en: The emperor would no longer fret from hunger, and the capital would see grain boats plying the canals again;
units.literal: The Son of Heaven will have no worry of sitting sideways on his mat; the capital populace will see boats passing to and fro;

units.zh: 四方旅拒者可以破膽，三河流離者於茲請命。
units.en: rebels in the provinces would lose heart, and refugees along the Yellow, Huai, and other rivers could beg for relief.
units.literal: those who resist from the four quarters can have their courage broken; those displaced along the Three Rivers can here plead for their lives.

units.zh: 相公匡戴明主，為富人侯，此今之切務，不可失也。
units.en: By supporting our enlightened sovereign you would become a great lord of wealth—this is the urgent task of the moment and must not be let slip.
units.literal: The Chancellor aids and supports the enlightened sovereign and becomes a marquis among wealthy men—this is today's urgent task and must not be missed.

units.zh: 使仆湔洗瑕穢，率罄愚懦，當憑經義，請護河堤，冥勤在官，不辭水死。
units.en: Give me leave to clear my name and give all my poor wits to the cause. On principle I ask to defend the river works myself, to labor at my post in silence, and not to shirk death by drowning.
units.literal: Enable this servant to wash away stains, lead with all my foolish timidity, rely on canonical principles, request to guard the river dikes, labor in office in obscurity, and not refuse death by water.

units.zh: 然運之利病，各有四五焉。
units.en: Yet transport has its own four or five advantages and as many drawbacks.
units.literal: Yet the profit and harm of transport each have four or five aspects.

units.zh: 晏自尹京入為計相，共五年矣。
units.en: I have been metropolitan governor and then chief fiscal officer for five years altogether.
units.literal: Yan, from governing the capital to becoming chief of finance, has served five years in all.

units.zh: 京師三輔百姓，唯苦稅畝傷多，若使江、湖米來每年三二十萬，即頓減徭賦，歌舞皇澤，其利一也。
units.en: The people around Chang'an groan under heavy land taxes; if two or three hundred thousand piculs of Jianghu grain arrived yearly, levies could drop at once and they would praise the throne's bounty—that is the first gain.
units.literal: The people of the capital and the Three Adjuncts suffer only from excessive land tax; if two or three hundred thousand piculs of grain from the rivers and lakes came each year, corvée and levies would be sharply reduced and they would sing of the sovereign's grace—this is the first benefit.

units.zh: 東都殘毀，百無一存。
units.en: The Eastern Capital is in ruins; scarcely one building in a hundred still stands.
units.literal: The Eastern Capital lies in ruins; not one part in a hundred remains.

units.zh: 若米運流通，則饑人皆附，村落邑厘，從此滋多。
units.en: If grain shipping revives, starving refugees will settle there and hamlets will spring up again.
units.literal: If grain transport flows freely, the hungry will all gather, and villages and hamlets will multiply from this.

units.zh: 受命之日引海陵之倉以食鞏、洛，是計之得者，其利二也。
units.en: From the day I took office I have drawn Hailing's stores to feed Gong and Luoyang—a sound plan and the second gain.
units.literal: From the day of my mandate I have drawn on the granaries of Hailing to feed Gong and Luo—this is a sound plan; that is the second benefit.

units.zh: 諸將有在邊者，諸戎有侵敗王略者，或聞三江、五湖，貢輸紅粒，雲帆桂楫，輸納帝鄉，軍誌曰：「先聲後實，可以震耀夷夏。」
units.en: Frontier generals and tribes that raid the borders, hearing that red grain from the Yangzi lakes is shipped on cloud-white sails and cassia-prowed boats to the capital, will recall the maxim that reputation should precede force—thus aweing both barbarian and Chinese.'
units.literal: Generals stationed on the frontier and barbarians who encroach on the imperial domain—when they hear that from the Three Rivers and Five Lakes red grain is presented in tribute, with cloudlike sails and cassia oars shipping it to the imperial capital, military doctrine says: 'Sound precedes substance; this can awe barbarians and Chinese alike.'

units.zh: 其利三也。
units.en: That is the third gain.
units.literal: That is the third benefit.

units.zh: 自古帝王之盛，皆云書同文，車同軌，日月所照，莫不率俾。
units.en: Since antiquity the height of imperial power has been described as one script, one track, and universal submission to the throne.
units.literal: From antiquity the glory of emperors has been described as identical script and identical wheel-gauge, and all beneath the sun and moon submitting in obedience.

units.zh: 今舟車既通，商賈往來，百貨雜集，航海梯山，聖神輝光，漸近貞觀、永徽之盛，其利四也。
units.en: With waterways and roads open again, merchants travel freely, goods pile up, and trade spans sea and mountain—the court's glory would approach the prosperity of the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras; that is the fourth gain.
units.literal: Now that boats and carts are connected, merchants come and go, goods of every kind gather, and trade crosses seas and mountains—the sage sovereign's radiance approaches the splendor of Zhenguan and Yonghui; that is the fourth benefit.

units.zh: 所可疑者，函、陜雕殘，東周尤甚。
units.en: What gives pause is the devastation of Hangu Pass and Shaan, worst of all in the old Eastern Zhou heartland.
units.literal: What gives pause is that Hangu and Shaan are carved to ruin, and the Eastern Zhou region is worst of all.

units.zh: 過宜陽、熊耳，至武牢、成臯，五百里中，編戶千余而已。
units.en: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, five hundred li hold barely a thousand registered households.
units.literal: From Yiyang and Xiong'er to Wulao and Chenggao, within five hundred li there are only a little over a thousand registered households.

units.zh: 居無尺椽，人無煙爨，蕭條淒慘，獸遊鬼哭。
units.en: Not a rafter stands, no hearth smoke rises; the land is desolate, beasts roam, and it seems ghosts wail.
units.literal: Homes lack a single rafter; people lack cooking smoke; desolation is bleak and beasts roam while ghosts seem to wail.

units.zh: 牛必羸角，輿必說輹，棧車輓漕，亦不易求。
units.en: Oxen are emaciated, cart wheels fall off, and even simple haulage carts are hard to find.
units.literal: Oxen are sure to be scrawny-horned, carts sure to have wheels come loose; even plank carts for haulage are not easily found.

units.zh: 今於無人之境，興此勞人之運，固難就矣，其病一也。
units.en: To launch this laborious transport through uninhabited country is bound to fail—that is the first drawback.
units.literal: To launch this labor-consuming transport in a land without people is inherently hard to accomplish—that is the first drawback.

units.zh: 河、汴有初，不修則毀澱，故每年正月發近縣丁男，塞長茭，決沮淤，清明桃花已後，遠水自然安流，陽侯、宓妃，不復太息。
units.en: The Yellow River and Bian Canal must be dredged yearly or they silt shut; each New Year laborers from nearby counties clear reeds and sediment, and after Qingming the distant reaches run clear again without the river gods' lament.
units.literal: The Yellow River and Bian Canal had their beginnings; if not maintained they silt up, so every first month conscript labor from nearby counties blocks long reeds and clears sediment; after Qingming and the peach blossoms, distant waters flow smoothly of themselves, and the River Lord and Lady Mi need sigh no more.

units.zh: 頃因寇難，總不掏拓，澤滅水，岸石崩，役夫需於沙，津吏旋於濘，千里洄上，罔水舟行，其病二也。
units.en: Since the rebellions dredging has stopped entirely; marshes have swallowed the channel, banks have collapsed, laborers wait on sandbars, clerks flounder in mud, and for a thousand li upstream boats cannot sail—that is the second drawback.
units.literal: Recently because of rebellion dredging has altogether ceased; marshes have swallowed the water, bank stones have collapsed, laborers wait on sandbars, ferry clerks turn in the mud, and for a thousand li upstream there is no water for boats—that is the second drawback.

units.zh: 東垣、底柱，澠池、二陵，北河運處五六百里，戍卒久絕，縣吏空拳。
units.en: From Dongyuan and Dizhu to Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li of the northern transport route have no garrisons left and county officials are powerless.
units.literal: From Dongyuan and Dizhu to Mianchi and the Two Mounds, five or six hundred li along the northern river transport route—garrison troops have long been cut off and county clerks are empty-handed.

units.zh: 奪攘奸宄，窟穴囊橐。
units.en: Bandits and outlaws raid and hide in caves with their plunder.
units.literal: Robbers and villains plunder and nest in caves with their loot.

units.zh: 夾河為藪，豺狼狺狺，舟行所經，寇亦能往，其病三也。
units.en: Marshes line the river, wolves howl, and wherever boats can go bandits can follow—that is the third drawback.
units.literal: Along the river are marshes; wolves and jackals snarl; wherever boats pass, bandits can also go—that is the third drawback.

units.zh: 東自淮陰，西臨蒲阪，亙三千里，屯戍相望。
units.en: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, three thousand li of garrisons stand face to face.
units.literal: From Huaiyin in the east to Pufan in the west, spanning three thousand li, garrisons face one another.

units.zh: 中軍皆鼎司元侯，賤卒儀同青紫，每雲食半菽，又雲無挾纊，輓漕所至，船到便留，即非單車使折簡書所能制矣，其病四也。
units.en: Central Army posts are held by chief ministers and great lords; common soldiers dress like officers; they claim to eat half rations and lack winter coats; wherever grain convoys arrive the boats are seized on the spot—not something a lone commissioner with a letter can restrain—that is the fourth drawback.
units.literal: Central Army posts are held by chief ministers and great marquises; lowly soldiers dress like the purple-clad elite; they always say they eat half beans and have no padded coats; wherever transport grain arrives, boats are detained on arrival—this is not something a lone envoy with a letter can control; that is the fourth drawback.

units.zh: 惟小子畢其慮奔走之，惟中書詳其利病裁成之。
units.en: I alone will give all my thought and effort to the task; only the Secretariat can weigh the pros and cons and bring the plan to completion.
units.literal: Only this humble servant will exhaust his thought and run about it; only the Secretariat will weigh profit and harm and complete the plan.

units.zh: 晏累年已來，事缺名毀，聖慈含育，特賜生全。
units.en: For years my duties were curtailed and my name slandered; the emperor's mercy spared my life.
units.literal: Yan for many years has had his duties cut short and his name slandered; the sage's compassion nurtured him and specially granted him life.

units.zh: 月余家居，遽即臨遣，恩榮感切，思殞百身。
units.en: After barely a month at home I was suddenly dispatched on imperial business; overwhelmed by grace, I would gladly die a hundred deaths in return.
units.literal: After a month at home he was suddenly sent on imperial mission; moved by grace and honor, he wished to die a hundred deaths in return.

units.zh: 見一水不通，願荷鍤而先往；
units.en: Wherever a channel was blocked I wished to take a spade and go first;
units.literal: seeing one waterway blocked, he wished to shoulder a spade and go first;

units.zh: 見一粒不運，願負米而先趨。
units.en: wherever a grain was not moved I wished to carry rice and hurry ahead.
units.literal: seeing one grain not transported, he wished to carry rice and hurry ahead.

units.zh: 焦心苦形，期報明主，丹誠未克，漕引多虞，屏營中流，掩泣獻狀。
units.en: I wore myself out in body and mind to repay my sovereign; my loyal effort had not yet succeeded and transport still faced many perils; pacing midstream in anxiety, I wept as I submitted this memorial.
units.literal: He tormented heart and body, hoping to repay the enlightened sovereign; his red sincerity had not yet succeeded, and grain transport had many worries; pacing anxiously midstream, he wept as he presented his memorial.

units.zh: 自此每歲運米數十萬石以濟關中。
units.en: From then on several hundred thousand piculs of grain were shipped yearly to supply Guanzhong.
units.literal: From this time each year several hundred thousand piculs of grain were transported to relieve Guanzhong.

units.zh: 始為朗州小校，唐廣明初，王仙芝焚劫江陵。
units.en: He began as a Langzhou corporal; when Wang Xianzhi sacked Jiangling in early Guangming,
units.literal: At first he was a petty officer of Lang prefecture; at the beginning of Tang Guangming, Wang Xianzhi burned and plundered Jiangling.

units.zh: 代宗踐祚，特嘉之，召拜工部尚書。
units.en: When Emperor Daizong took the throne he singled Guozhen out for praise and summoned him to court as minister of works.
units.literal: When Daizong ascended the throne he especially commended him and summoned him to court as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 代宗聞其事，悼惜久之。
units.en: When Daizong heard the news, he grieved for him a long while.
units.literal: When Daizong heard, he mourned him a long while.

units.zh: 大歷五年四月，會月給糧儲，兵馬使臧玠與判官達奚覯忿爭，覯曰：「今幸無事。」
units.en: In the fourth month of 770, at the monthly distribution of grain stores, army commissioner Zang Zhi quarreled with legal aide Daxi Gun. Gun said, "For the moment all is well."
units.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Dali, at the monthly issue of grain stores, the army commissioner Zang Zhi quarreled with the legal aide Daxi Gun. Gun said, "For now there is nothing amiss."

units.zh: 宰相皇甫鎛方諛媚固寵，道古言柳泌有道術，鎛得進之，待詔翰林。
units.en: Chief Minister Huangfu Bo was then currying favor through flattery. Daogu claimed that Liu Bi possessed Daoist arts. Bo presented him to the throne, and Liu was retained at the Hanlin Academy.
units.literal: Chief minister Huangfu Bo was then flattering to secure favor; Daogu said Liu Bi possessed the Way and its arts; Bo was able to present him, and he awaited edicts at the Hanlin Academy.

units.zh: 鎛既貶責，授道古循州司馬，終以服丹藥，歐血而卒。
units.en: After Bo was demoted and punished, Daogu was appointed acting chief secretary of Xun Prefecture. He ultimately died vomiting blood from the elixirs he had taken.
units.literal: After Bo was demoted and censured, Daogu was appointed acting chief secretary of Xunzhou; in the end, because he had taken elixir drugs, he vomited blood and died.

units.zh: 憲宗季年頗信方士，銳於服食，詔天下搜訪奇士。
units.en: In his later years Emperor Xianzong placed great faith in alchemists and eagerly pursued elixirs of immortality. He ordered an empire-wide search for wonder-workers.
units.literal: In Xianzong's late years he greatly trusted alchemical masters, was keen on ingesting elixirs; he decreed searching the empire for extraordinary men.

units.zh: 元和十三年，入為宗正卿。
units.en: In 818 he was recalled to the capital as director of the Directorate for Imperial Clansmen.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, he entered [the capital] as director of the Directorate for Imperial Clansmen.

units.zh: 穆宗在東宮，扼腕於其事，及居喪，皆竄逐誅之。
units.en: While still heir apparent, Muzong had been deeply troubled by these events. Once he assumed the throne in mourning, he banished or executed all those involved.
units.literal: Muzong, while in the Eastern Palace, wrung his hands over this affair; when he entered mourning on ascending the throne, he banished or executed them all.

units.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。
units.en: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as right regular attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。
units.en: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.
units.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
units.en: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Academy, commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and commissioner for salt and iron transport across all circuits.
units.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Academy, Commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport across all circuits.

units.zh: 太宗因修禮官奏事之次，言及喪服，太宗曰：「又舅之與姨，親疏相似，而服紀有殊，理未為得。宜集學者詳議。餘有親重而服輕者，亦附奏聞。」於是侍中魏徵、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等奏議曰：臣聞禮所以決嫌疑，定猶豫，別同異，明是非者也。非從天降，非從地出，人情而已矣。夫親族有九，服術有六，隨恩以薄厚，稱情以立文。然舅之與姨，雖為同氣，論情度義，先後實殊。何則？舅為母之本族，姨乃外戚他族，求之母族，姨不在焉，考之經典，舅誠為重。故周王念齊，每稱舅甥之國；秦伯懷晉，實切《渭陽》之詩。在舅服止一時，為姨居喪五月，循名喪實，逐末棄本。蓋古人之情，或有未達，所宜損益，實在茲乎！《記》曰：「兄弟之子，猶子也。蓋引而進之也；嫂叔之不服，蓋推而遠之也。」禮：繼父同居，則為之期；未嘗同居，則不為服。從母之夫，舅之妻，二夫人相為服。或曰，同爨緦。然則繼父之徒，並非骨肉，服重由乎同爨，恩輕在乎異居。故知制服雖繫於名；亦緣恩之厚薄者也。或有長年之嫂，遇孩童之叔，劬勞鞠養，情若新生，分飢共寒，契闊偕老。譬同居之繼父，方他人之同爨，情義之深淺，寧可同日而言哉！在其生也，愛之同於骨肉；及其死也，則曰推而遠之。求之本原，深所未諭。若推而遠之為是，則不可生而共居；生而共居之為是，則不可死同行路。重其生而輕其死，厚其始而薄其終，稱情立文，其義安在？且事嫂見稱，載籍非一。鄭仲虞則恩禮甚篤，顏弘都則竭誠致感，馬援則見之必冠，孔伋則哭之為位。此並躬踐教義，仁深孝友，察其所尚之旨，豈非先覺者歟？但於其時，上無哲王，禮非下之所議，遂使深情郁乎千載，至理藏於萬古，其來久矣，豈不惜哉！今屬欽明在辰，聖人有作，五禮詳洽，一物無遺。猶且永念慎終，凝神遐想。以為尊卑之敘，雖煥乎大備；喪紀之制，或情理未周。爰命秩宗，更詳考正。臣等奏遵明旨，觸類旁求，採摭群經，討論傳記。或引兼名實，無文之禮咸秩，惇睦之情畢舉，變薄俗於既往，垂篤義於將來，信六籍所不能談，超百王而獨得者也。諸儒所守，互有異同，詳求厥中，申明聖旨。謹按曾祖父母舊服齊衰三月，請加為齊衰五月。嫡子婦舊服大功，請加為期。眾子婦小功，今請與兄弟子婦同為大功九月。嫂叔舊無服，今請服小功五月報。其弟妻及夫兄，亦小功五月。舅服緦麻，請與從母同服小功。
units.en: While Taizong was hearing the ritual-revision officers report on business, the subject reached mourning dress. Taizong said: "Also, maternal uncles and maternal aunts are similar in closeness, yet the mourning regulations differ for them; in principle this does not seem right. Scholars should be assembled to deliberate on it in detail. Other cases where kinship is heavy but mourning is light should also be appended and reported." Thereupon Palace Attendant Wei Zheng, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others memorialized in deliberation: Your servants have heard that ritual is what resolves doubts and suspicions, settles hesitations, distinguishes sameness and difference, and clarifies right and wrong. It does not descend from Heaven or emerge from earth; it is simply human feeling. Kin have nine degrees and mourning techniques have six, thinning or thickening according to affection and establishing the text according to feeling. Yet although maternal uncle and maternal aunt are of the same breath, when feeling is discussed and obligation measured, the former and latter are truly different. Why? The maternal uncle belongs to the mother's root clan, while the maternal aunt is an external relative of another clan. Seeking within the mother's clan, the maternal aunt is not there; examining the classics, the maternal uncle is truly weighty. Therefore when the Zhou king remembered Qi, he always called it the state of uncle and nephew; when the Earl of Qin cherished Jin, it was truly close to the poem Weiyang. For a maternal uncle, mourning stops at one season; for a maternal aunt, one mourns five months. This follows the name and loses the substance, pursuing the branch and abandoning the root. The feeling of the ancients perhaps had something not yet fully reached, and what should be reduced or increased truly lies here. The Record says: "The sons of brothers are like sons; this draws them in and advances them. That elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law do not mourn each other pushes them away." In ritual, for a stepfather who has lived with one, one wears one-year mourning; if he has never lived with one, one wears no mourning. A mother's sister's husband and a maternal uncle's wife, these two spouses mourn one another. Some say that those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp. Thus stepfathers and such are not flesh and blood, yet mourning is heavy because of sharing the hearth, and affection is light because of living apart. Therefore we know that although mourning dress depends on names, it also follows the thickness or thinness of affection. Sometimes there is an elder sister-in-law of advanced years with a younger brother-in-law who was a child; she toiled to raise him, with feeling as if newly giving birth, sharing hunger and cold, and staying with him through hardship into old age. Compared with a stepfather who shared the household or with another person sharing the cooking hearth, how could the depth or shallowness of feeling and obligation be discussed on the same day? While she lives, he loves her as flesh and blood; when she dies, one says she is pushed away. Seeking the root of this, we deeply fail to understand it. If pushing away is right, then they should not live together while alive. If living together while alive is right, then they cannot be treated as people on the road when dead. To value the living and slight the dead, to thicken the beginning and thin the end: where is the meaning of matching feeling and establishing text? Moreover, serving a sister-in-law is praised in more than one written record. Zheng Zhongyu's grace and ritual were very deep; Yan Hongdu exhausted sincerity and produced a response; Ma Yuan always put on his cap when seeing his sister-in-law; Kong Ji cried for his sister-in-law with a set position. These all personally practiced teaching and obligation, with benevolence deep in filial and fraternal feeling. Examining the purpose of what they honored, were they not those who awakened first? Only in their time there was no wise king above, and ritual was not for those below to debate; thus deep feeling was suppressed for a thousand years, and perfect principle was hidden for ten thousand ages. This has been so for a long time; is it not regrettable? Now we meet a time when reverent brightness is present and a sage has arisen. The five rites are detailed and complete, with not one thing omitted. Still Your Majesty forever thinks on careful endings and concentrates spirit in distant reflection, considering that although the sequence of honored and lowly is bright and fully prepared, the regulations of mourning may not yet be complete in feeling and principle. Therefore you ordered the Minister of Rites to examine and correct them in more detail. Your servants, in memorializing, follow the bright command, seek sideways by analogy, gather from the many classics, and discuss commentaries and records. Some cases draw on both name and substance; rites without written text are all ordered, and the feeling of generous harmony is fully raised, changing thin customs from the past and transmitting deep obligation to the future. This is truly what the six classics could not discuss and what surpasses the hundred kings as Your Majesty's sole attainment. The various scholars hold to different views. We have sought the center in detail and extend and clarify the sage command. Respectfully, the old mourning for great-grandparents was three months of trimmed mourning; we request increasing it to five months of trimmed mourning. The old mourning for the principal son's wife was great-work mourning; we request increasing it to one year. The mourning for wives of other sons was small-work mourning; we now request making it the same as for brothers' sons' wives, great-work mourning for nine months. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law formerly had no mourning; we now request reciprocal small-work mourning for five months. The younger brother's wife and her husband's elder brother should also have small-work mourning for five months. Mourning for a maternal uncle was fine hemp; we request making it the same as for a mother's sister, small-work mourning.

units.zh: 貞觀年中，八座議奏：『舅服同姨，小功五月。』
units.en: In Zhenguan the Eight Seats had ruled that mourning for a mother's brother matched that for a mother's sister: five months' lesser accomplishment.
units.literal: In the Zhenguan era the Eight Seats deliberated and memorialized: 'For the mother's brother, mourning is the same as for the mother's sister—five months' lesser accomplishment.

units.zh: 刑部郎中田再思建議曰：干尊坤卑，天一地二，陰陽之位分矣，夫婦之道配焉。至若死喪之威，隆殺之等，禮經五服之制，齊斬有殊，考妣三年之喪，貴賤無隔，以報免懷之慈，以酬罔極之恩者也。稽之上古，喪期無數，暨乎中葉，方有歲年。《禮》云：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異代，不相襲禮。」《白虎通》云：「質文再變，正朔三而復。」自周公制禮之後，孔父刊經已來，爰殊厭降之儀，以標服紀之節。重輕從俗，斟酌隨時。故知禮不從天而降，不由地而出也，在人消息，為適時之中耳。春秋諸國，魯最知禮，以周公之後，孔子之邦也。晉韓起來聘，言「周禮盡在魯矣。」齊仲孫來盟，言「魯猶秉周禮。」尚有子張問高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂同母異父昆弟之服大功，子夏謂合從齊衰之制。此等並四科之數，十哲之人，高步孔門，親承聖訓，及遇喪事，猶此致疑，即明自古已來，升降不一者也。三年之制，說者紛然。鄭玄以為二十七月，王肅以為二十五月。又改葬之服，鄭云服緦三月，王云訖葬而除。又繼母出嫁，鄭云皆服，王云從於繼育，乃為之服。又無服之殤，鄭云子生一月，哭之一日；王云以哭之一日易服之月。鄭、王祖經宗傳，各有異同；荀摯采古求遺，互為損益。方知去聖漸遠，殘缺彌多。故曰會禮之家，名為聚訟，寧有定哉！而父在為母三年，行之已逾四紀，出自高宗大帝之代，不從則天皇后之朝。大帝御極之辰，中宮獻書之日，往時參議，將可施行，編之於格，服之已久。前王所是，疏而為律；後王所是，著而為令。何必乖先帝之旨，阻人子之情，虧純孝之心，背德義之本？有何妨於聖化，有何紊於彝倫，而欲服之週年，與伯叔母齊焉，與姑姊妹同焉？夫三年之喪，如白駒之過隙，君子喪親，有終身之憂，何況再周乎！夫禮者，體也，履也，示之以跡。孝者，畜也，養也，因之以心。小人不恥不仁，不畏不義。服之有制，使愚人企及；衣之以衰，使見之摧痛。以此防人，人猶有朝死而夕忘者；以此制人，人猶有釋服而從吉者。方今漸歸古樸，須敦孝義，抑賢引愚，理資寧戚，食稻衣錦，所不忍聞。若以庶事朝儀，一依周禮，則古之人臣見君也，公卿大夫贄羔雁、珪璧，今何故不依乎？周之用刑也，墨、劓、宮、刖，今何故不行乎？周則侯、甸、男、衛，朝聘有數，今何故不行乎？周則不五十不仕，七十不入朝，今何故不依乎？周則井、邑、丘、甸，以立徵稅，今何故不行乎？周則三老五等，父死子及，今何故不行乎？周則冠冕衣裘，乘車而戰，今何故不行乎？周則分土五更，膠序養老，今何故不行乎？諸如此例，不可勝述。何獨孝思之事，愛一年之服於其母乎？可為痛心，可為慟哭者！《詩》云：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。」《禮》云：「父之親子也，親賢而下無能；母之親子也，賢則親之，無能則憐之。」阮嗣宗晉代之英才，方外之高士，以為母重於父。據齊斬升數，粗細已降，何忍服之節制，減至於周？豈後代之士，盡慚於古。循古未必是，依今未必非也。又同爨服緦，禮經明義。嫂叔遠別，同諸路人。引而進之，觸類而長。猶子咸衣苴枲，季父不服緦麻，推遠之情有餘，睦親之義未足。又母之昆弟，情切渭陽，翟酺訟舅之冤，甯氏宅甥之相，我之出也，義亦殷焉。不同從母之尊，遂降小功之服，依諸古禮，有爽俗情。今貶舅而宗姨，是陋今而榮古。此並太宗之制也，行之百年矣，輒為刊復，實用有疑。
units.en: Tian Zaisi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, made a proposal: Qian is honored and kun is lowly; Heaven is one and earth is two. The positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired with them. As for the awe of death and mourning and the grades of fullness and reduction, the ritual classics have the system of the five mourning grades. Trimmed and unhemmed mourning differ, but the three-year mourning for father and mother has no barrier between noble and base, because it repays the kindness of bearing and cherishing and answers boundless grace. Examining high antiquity, mourning terms had no fixed number; by middle antiquity, only then were there years and months. The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in time and did not follow one another in music; the Three Kings differed in age and did not inherit one another's rites." The Baihu Tong says: "Plainness and refinement change twice, and the first month changes through three and returns." Since the Duke of Zhou made ritual and since Confucius edited the classics, there have been different rules of suppression and reduction to mark the divisions of mourning regulations. Heavy and light follow custom; deliberation and adjustment follow the time. Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. Based on the thread counts of trimmed and unhemmed mourning, coarseness and fineness already descend. How can one bear for the term of mourning to be reduced to one year? Surely later men are not all ashamed before antiquity. Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following the present is not necessarily wrong. Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.
units.literal: Tian Zaisi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, made a proposal: Qian is honored and kun is lowly; Heaven is one and earth is two. The positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired with them. As for the awe of death and mourning and the grades of fullness and reduction, the ritual classics have the system of the five mourning grades. Trimmed and unhemmed mourning differ, but the three-year mourning for father and mother has no barrier between noble and base, because it repays the kindness of bearing and cherishing and answers boundless grace. Examining high antiquity, mourning terms had no fixed number; by middle antiquity, only then were there years and months. The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in time and did not follow one another in music; the Three Kings differed in age and did not inherit one another's rites." The Baihu Tong says: "Plainness and refinement change twice, and the first month changes through three and returns." Since the Duke of Zhou made ritual and since Confucius edited the classics, there have been different rules of suppression and reduction to mark the divisions of mourning regulations. Heavy and light follow custom; deliberation and adjustment follow the time. Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.

units.zh: 制可之。
units.en: The throne approved.
units.literal: The ordinance approved it.

units.zh: 宣宗擢為同州刺史。
units.en: Emperor Xuanzong appointed him prefect of Tong.
units.literal: Emperor Xuanzong promoted him to prefect of Tong.

units.zh: 憲宗立，權綱自出，頔稍懼，願以子尚主，帝許之。
units.en: When Xianzong came to the throne and power flowed from the center again, Di grew uneasy and offered his son in marriage to a princess; the emperor agreed.
units.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne and authority issued from him alone, Di grew somewhat afraid and wished to marry his son to a princess; the emperor consented.

units.zh: 季友尚憲宗永昌公主，拜駙馬都尉。
units.en: Jiyou married Xianzong's Princess Yongchang and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.
units.literal: Jiyou married Emperor Xianzong's Princess Yongchang and was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Sons-in-Law.

units.zh: 帝討蔡，頔獻家財以助國，帝卻之。
units.en: When the emperor campaigned against Cai, Di offered his family fortune to support the war effort, but the emperor refused.
units.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Cai, Di offered his family wealth to aid the state; the emperor declined it.

units.zh: 帝初欲頔告老，宰相李逢吉謂得謝乃優禮，非所以示責。
units.en: The emperor first wanted Di to retire, but Chief Minister Li Fengji argued that granting retirement would look like an honor, not a punishment.
units.literal: The emperor at first wished Di to request retirement; Chief Minister Li Fengji said that granting leave would be a mark of favor, not a way to show censure.

units.zh: 宰司將以太子少保官之，帝改署賓客。
units.en: The chief ministers planned to make him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, but the emperor reassigned him as Retainer instead.
units.literal: The chief ministers were about to appoint him Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent; the emperor changed the appointment to Retainer.

units.zh: 憲宗遣中使問狀，具對府政苛細，力不堪奉。
units.en: Xianzong dispatched an imperial messenger to investigate; Gao explained in full that the prefect's rule was petty and exacting beyond what he could endure.
units.literal: Emperor Xianzong sent a palace envoy to inquire into the matter; he fully replied that the prefectural administration was harsh and meticulous and his strength could not bear service.

units.zh: 代還，坐治第過制，憲宗薄不用，改光祿卿。
units.en: On recall he was charged with building a residence that exceeded regulations; Xianzong looked on him coldly and reassigned him as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: When replaced and recalled, he was charged with building a residence exceeding regulations; Xianzong held him in low regard and did not employ him, and he was changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 陳少遊，博州人也。
units.en: Chen Shaoyou was a native of Bozhou.
units.literal: Chen Shaoyou was a native of Bozhou.

units.zh: 父慶，右武衛兵曹參軍，以少遊累贈工部尚書。
units.en: His father Qing had been a military staff officer of the Right Martial Guards; because of Shaoyou he was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of Public Works.
units.literal: His father Qing was a military staff officer of the Right Martial Guards; because of Shaoyou he was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of Public Works.

units.zh: 少遊幼聰辯，初習《莊》、《列》、《老子》，為崇玄館學生，眾推引講經。
units.en: Shaoyou was clever and eloquent as a youth. He first studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, entered the Chongxuan Hall as a student, and his fellows recommended him to lecture on the classics.
units.literal: Shaoyou was clever and eloquent in youth; he first studied the Zhuangzi, Liezi, and Laozi, became a student of the Chongxuan Hall, and the crowd recommended him to expound the classics.

units.zh: 秀遽曰：「中丞美才，不當遠官，請從容旬日，冀竭蹇分。」
units.en: Xiu said hastily, "Vice Censor, your talent is too fine for a distant post. Give me ten days or so; I hope to do what little I can."
units.literal: Xiu said hastily: "Vice Censor, your talent is too fine for a distant post. Please allow ten days or so; I hope to do my poor utmost."

units.zh: 既擢第，補渝州南平令，理甚有聲。
units.en: After passing the examination he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou, where his governance won wide renown.
units.literal: After he passed the examination he was appointed magistrate of Nanping in Yuzhou, and his governance won great renown.

units.zh: 至德中，河東節度王思禮奏為參謀，累授大理司直、監察殿中侍御史、節度判官。
units.en: In the Zhide era Wang Sili, military commissioner of Hedong, recommended him as staff adviser. He rose through appointments as rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.
units.literal: In the Zhide era Wang Sili, military commissioner of Hedong, memorialized that he be made staff adviser; he was repeatedly appointed rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review, investigating palace censor, and military commissioner aide.

units.zh: 寶應元年，入為金部員外郎。
units.en: In the first year of Baoying he entered court as outer office director in the Ministry of Revenue.
units.literal: In the first year of Baoying he entered court as outer office director in the Ministry of Revenue.

units.zh: 無幾，澤潞節度使李抱玉表為副使、御史中丞、陳鄭二州留後。
units.en: Before long Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, recommended him as deputy commissioner, Censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng.
units.literal: Before long Li Baoyu, military commissioner of Zelu, memorialized that he be made deputy commissioner, Censor-in-chief, and acting governor of Chen and Zheng.

units.zh: 遷晉州刺史，改同州刺史，未視事，又歷晉、鄭二州刺史。
units.en: He was made prefect of Jinzhou, then reassigned to Tongzhou. Before he could take up that post he served again as prefect of Jin and Zheng.
units.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Jinzhou, then changed to prefect of Tongzhou; before taking office he again served as prefect of Jin and Zheng.

units.zh: 其年，除桂州刺史、桂管觀察使。
units.en: That year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Gui circuit.
units.literal: That year he was appointed prefect of Guizhou and observation commissioner of the Gui circuit.

units.zh: 秀、載內外引薦，數日，拜宣州刺史、宣歙池都團練觀察使。
units.en: With recommendations from Xiu within the palace and Zai outside it, within a few days he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training-and-defense and observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.
units.literal: Xiu and Zai recommended him inside and outside court; within a few days he was appointed prefect of Xuanzhou and overall training-and-defense and observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi.

units.zh: 及會，少遊攝齊升坐，音韻清辯，觀者屬目。
units.en: When the day came, Shaoyou gathered his robes and ascended the seat. His voice was clear and his argument keen, and every eye in the hall was on him.
units.literal: When the meeting came, Shaoyou gathered his robes and ascended the seat; his tones were clear and his argument keen, and the onlookers fixed their eyes on him.

units.zh: 祖儼，安西副都護。
units.en: His grandfather Yan had served as Vice Protector-general of Anxi.
units.literal: His grandfather Yan was Vice Protector-general of Anxi.

units.zh: 明年，仆固懷恩奏為河北副元帥判官、兵部郎中、兼侍御史。
units.en: The following year Pugu Huai'en recommended him as aide to the deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, bureau director in the Ministry of War, and concurrent attendant censor.
units.literal: The next year Pugu Huai'en memorialized that he be made aide to the deputy commander-in-chief of Hebei, bureau director in the Ministry of War, and concurrent attendant censor.

units.zh: 永泰二年，抱玉又奏為隴右行軍司馬，拜檢校左庶子，依前兼中丞。
units.en: In the second year of Yongtai, Baoyu again recommended him as marching army vice marshal of Longyou and acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, while retaining his concurrent post as Censor-in-chief.
units.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, Baoyu again memorialized that he be made marching army vice marshal of Longyou, appointed acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and as before concurrently Censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 所引文句，悉兼他義，諸生不能對，甚為大學士陳希烈所嘆賞，又以同宗，遇之甚厚。
units.en: Every passage he cited carried additional meanings, and the students could not answer him. Grand Academician Chen Xilie greatly admired him, and because they shared the same surname clan, treated him with exceptional favor.
units.literal: The passages he cited all carried additional meanings; the students could not reply, and Grand Academician Chen Xilie greatly admired him; moreover, being of the same clan, he treated him very generously.

units.zh: 尋授侍御史、迥紇糧料使，改檢校職方員外郎。
units.en: Soon he was made attendant censor and grain-supply commissioner for the Uyghurs, and was reassigned as acting outer office director in the Ministry of War.
units.literal: Soon he was made attendant censor and grain-supply commissioner for the Uyghurs, and was changed to acting outer office director in the Ministry of War.

units.zh: 充使檢校郎官，自少遊始也。
units.en: The practice of appointing an envoy with acting courtier rank began with Shaoyou.
units.literal: Serving as envoy with acting courtier rank began with Shaoyou.

units.zh: 少遊為理，長於權變，時推幹濟，然厚斂財貨，交結權幸，以是頻獲遷擢。
units.en: In governing, Shaoyou was skilled at expedient adaptation and was praised for practical ability. Yet he levied heavy taxes, cultivated the powerful and favored at court, and thereby won frequent promotion.
units.literal: Shaoyou in governing was skilled in expedient adaptation; his contemporaries praised his practical ability, yet he heavily levied wealth and cultivated connections with the powerful and favored, and thereby frequently gained promotion.

units.zh: 少遊以嶺僥遐遠，欲規求近郡。
units.en: Shaoyou, finding the Ling region remote and arduous, set about securing a post nearer the capital.
units.literal: Shaoyou, because the Ling region was remote and perilous, wished to scheme for a nearer prefecture.

units.zh: 時中官董秀掌樞密用事，少遊乃宿於其裏，候其下直，際晚謁之，從容曰：「七郎家中人數幾何？
units.en: At that time the eunuch Dong Xiu controlled secret affairs and wielded great power. Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he left duty, and at dusk called on him. Calmly he asked, "Seventh Brother, how large is your household?
units.literal: At that time the eunuch Dong Xiu controlled secret affairs and wielded power; Shaoyou lodged in his lane, waited until he left duty, and at dusk called on him, saying calmly: "Seventh Brother, how many people are in your household?

units.zh: 時少遊又已納賄於元載子仲武矣。
units.en: By then Shaoyou had also paid bribes to Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.
units.literal: At that time Shaoyou had also paid bribes to Yuan Zai's son Zhongwu.

units.zh: 秀既逾於始望，欣愜頗甚，因與之厚相結。
units.en: Xiu, far beyond what he had first hoped for, was greatly pleased and formed a close bond with him.
units.literal: Xiu, exceeding his first hopes, was greatly pleased and formed a close bond with him.

units.zh: 每月所費復幾何？」
units.en: And how much do you spend each month?"
units.literal: How much do you spend each month?"

units.zh: 少遊曰：「據此之費，俸錢不足支數日，其餘常須數求外人，方可取濟。
units.en: Shaoyou said, "At that rate your salary would not last a few days. The rest must constantly be sought from outsiders before you can make ends meet.
units.literal: Shaoyou said: "By this reckoning your salary would not last a few days; the rest must constantly be sought from outsiders before you can make ends meet.

units.zh: 倘有輸誠供億者，但留心庇覆之，固易為力耳。
units.en: If someone offers you sincere support, you need only take him under your protection—it is easily done.
units.literal: If someone offers sincere support in supplying your needs, you need only take care to shelter him—it is easy enough to manage.

units.zh: 少遊雖不才，請以一身獨供七郎之費，每歲請獻錢五萬貫。
units.en: Though I lack talent, I ask to supply all of Seventh Brother's expenses myself, offering fifty thousand strings of cash each year.
units.literal: Though I am without talent, I ask to supply Seventh Brother's expenses alone myself, offering fifty thousand strings of cash each year.

units.zh: 今見有大半，請即受納，餘到官續送。
units.en: I have more than half of it on hand now—please accept it at once. The rest I will send once I take up my post.
units.literal: I now have more than half on hand—please accept it at once; the rest I will continue sending once I take office.

units.zh: 免貴人勞慮，不亦可乎？」
units.en: Would that not spare you worry?"
units.literal: Would it not spare a nobleman's anxieties?"

units.zh: 少遊言訖，泣曰：「南方炎瘴，深愴違辭，但恐不生還再睹顏色矣。」
units.en: When Shaoyou had finished he wept and said, "The southern heat and miasma grieve me deeply at this parting. I fear I shall not return alive to see you again."
units.literal: When Shaoyou finished speaking he wept and said: "The southern heat and miasma deeply grieve me at parting; I fear I shall not return alive to see your face again."
